chapters.title: Platforms, Payments and Getting Paid
chapters.subtitle: Build the money pipes before you open the tap
chapters.mentor_intro: A sale that never reaches your M-Pesa is not a sale. It is a number on a screen. So before we build pages or post a single video, we build the **money pipes** (os canos do dinheiro). That means the checkout that takes the payment, the products inside it, and the tests that prove the money really travels from a buyer in Brazil to your account in Mozambique. I will be honest with you: this is the least exciting chapter in the book. Nobody posts screenshots of their identity-check form. But this chapter protects every other one. If the pipes leak, more traffic just means bigger leaks. You will set up EscalePay as your main checkout and open Hotmart as your second channel and backup. You will learn the fee maths, so you know what you really keep. And you will cover the legal basics for Brazil, Portugal and Mozambique. Some platform facts are still unverified, so you will check them yourself, with small real tests, before you invite anyone to buy. A small test now gives you big protection later.
learning_goals: Set up EscalePay with all Family 1 products, BRL prices, delivery files and affiliate rules.
Run real verification tests (Pix, card, refund, payout) and record the results.
Calculate what you really keep from each sale on each platform.
Open a Hotmart producer account as your second channel and backup.
Apply the legal basics for Brazil, the EU and Mozambique, and prepare questions for an accountant.

sections.heading: EscalePay step by step: from account to products

blocks.text: EscalePay is your main **checkout** (página de pagamento). The company says it sells in 190 countries, accepts cards, Pix, Google Pay and Apple Pay, and supports affiliates, order bumps and one-click upsells. It also says it offers 7-day refunds and pays out to M-Pesa, e-Mola or a bank in meticais (MZN). Read that list again with one word in mind: **claims**. The operator is GRUPO DIGITALIZE LLC, with a Wyoming registered-agent address. Its international selling has **not been independently verified**. We do not know its currencies, the **FX spread** (spread cambial: the hidden exchange cost), how long payouts take, whether it holds money (retenção de saldo) or how it handles chargebacks. That is not a reason to panic. It is a reason to test. Do this now: copy that list into a Google Sheet and write 'CLAIM' next to each line. You change a line to 'TESTED' only when your own test proves it.

blocks.title: Set up the account
items: Create your account with your real name and an email you check every day. Use a strong password and turn on two-step login if it is offered.
Complete **KYC** (verificação de identidade): upload your ID and proof of address exactly as asked. Keep copies in a private folder.
Add your **payout method** (forma de saque / levantamento): M-Pesa, e-Mola or a bank account in MZN. The name must match your ID.
Fill in your seller details: name, contact email and the identification the platform asks for. You will reuse these on your legal pages.
Set every product price in **BRL** (reais). Your first buyers are Brazilian, and they think in reais.
Create the products in the order shown in the table below. Create the bundle last.

blocks.title: Delivery files
blocks.text: For each product, upload the final PDF and give it a clear name, like 'Caderno-do-Casal-52-Encontros.pdf'. During your test purchase, open the delivered file **on a phone**. Keep the master files (arquivos originais) in two places: your laptop and a cloud folder. A wrong or broken file is the fastest way to get refund requests.

blocks.title: Affiliate settings
blocks.text: Set **50% commission on front products only**, as planned in your affiliate kit. Before you invite any affiliate (afiliado), ask EscalePay two things in writing. First: is the commission calculated on the full price or on the price after fees? Second: does the affiliate also earn on the bump and the upsell? Both questions are in the support script in the next section. Write both answers in your sheet. Affiliates trust producers who explain the rules clearly.

sections.heading: Prove it works: the five verification tests

blocks.text: A **test purchase** (compra teste) is a real purchase, with real money, by a real buyer, that you follow from start to finish. Not the preview button. Not a fake card. The cost is small: one R$27 product, which is refunded afterwards. What you learn is huge, because it shows you what a Brazilian buyer really sees, and whether your money really arrives. One rule: mark every test as **TEST** in your sheet. A test purchase is never a sale you count, and never something you show as proof to buyers or affiliates.

blocks.title: The five tests
items: **Pix test:** ask a Brazilian contact to buy the front product with Pix from their own bank app. Ask for screenshots of every screen.

**Card test:** make one purchase by card (your contact's card, or your own international card if support confirms that seller test purchases are allowed). Note if it was accepted and if any extra fee appeared.
**What the buyer sees:** in the screenshots, check the currency, the exact price, the checkout language, whether the bump appears, and whether the access email arrives in Portuguese.

**Payout timing:** write down the date and hour of the sale. Request a withdrawal as soon as the balance allows. Write down when the money reaches M-Pesa, e-Mola or your bank, and how many MT arrived.

**Refund test:** request a refund for one test purchase through the platform. Note how many days it took and confirm with your contact that the money really came back. If it does not come back, pay your contact yourself, as you promised.

blocks.title: Mensagem para o seu contato brasileiro (PT-BR)
blocks.text: Oi, [nome]! Tudo bem? Estou lançando um produto digital para o Brasil e preciso fazer um teste real de pagamento antes de divulgar. Você poderia comprar um e-book de R$27 pelo Pix, usando o link que vou te mandar? O valor volta para você pelo reembolso da plataforma. Se não voltar, eu mesmo te devolvo. Se puder, tira print de cada tela: a página de pagamento, o valor, o comprovante do Pix e o e-mail de acesso. Isso vai me ajudar demais. Muito obrigado!

blocks.title: Perguntas para o suporte da EscalePay (por escrito)
blocks.text:
Olá! Antes de começar a vender, gostaria de confirmar por escrito as informações abaixo:
1) Qual é a taxa exata por venda: 10% ou 8% + USD 0,50? Existem outras taxas (saque, câmbio)?
2) O comprador brasileiro paga em reais (BRL) no Pix e no cartão?
3) Qual taxa de câmbio e qual spread vocês usam no saque para MZN (M-Pesa, e-Mola ou banco)?
4) Em quantos dias o saldo fica disponível? Existe retenção de saldo?
5) Como funcionam os reembolsos e os chargebacks? Quem paga a taxa de chargeback?
6) A comissão do afiliado é calculada sobre o preço cheio ou sobre o valor líquido? O afiliado também recebe comissão no order bump e no upsell?
7) Como devo mostrar minha identificação de vendedor ao comprador (Decreto 7.962/2013)?
8) Posso fazer uma compra de teste no meu próprio produto, com o meu cartão?
Agradeço desde já.

Do not send traffic, affiliates or ads to any checkout that has not passed the Pix test, the card test **and one real payout**. If the payout is slow, unclear or stuck, stop and use Hotmart while you investigate. Save every support answer as a screenshot. A promise in a chat window that disappears is not a promise.

sections.heading: Hotmart: your second channel and backup

blocks.text: Why a second platform if EscalePay works? First, **trust**: many Brazilian buyers already know Hotmart and feel safe paying there. Second, the **affiliate marketplace** (mercado de afiliados): affiliates in Brazil look for products to promote there, with commissions from 30% to 80%. Third, the boring reason: if one platform freezes your account, you still have a checkout that works.

blocks.title: What we know about Hotmart
items: It accepts producers outside Brazil and sells in 188 countries.
Brazil fee: **9.9% + R$2,49** per sale. The R$2,49 fixed part has applied since 21 Sep 2026. Confirm at signup which fee applies to you as a foreign producer.
Foreign producers are paid via **Payoneer in USD**. Third-party sources mention about 2% to withdraw and up to 2.75% for currency conversion. Check this at signup.
November (Black Friday 27 Nov 2026) is Hotmart's strongest month and January is second. Be ready on both platforms before November.

blocks.title: Payoneer in numbers (example only)
blocks.text: Imagine Hotmart sends you USD 100 (a fictional number). If the withdrawal costs about 2% and the conversion up to 2.75%, you could lose up to about USD 4.75 on the way. You keep about USD 95. This is why you check these numbers at signup, not after your first good month.

blocks.title: Platforms that are not for you (yet)
blocks.text: Kiwify needs a Brazilian CPF and a Brazilian bank account, so skip it for now. Lemon Squeezy reportedly supports Mozambique via PayPal, but it is being folded into Stripe Managed Payments. Gumroad reportedly does not support Mozambique. Keep your energy on **EscalePay plus Hotmart**. Do this now: open your Hotmart producer account this week, so the verification is done before you need it.

sections.heading: Fee maths: what you really keep

blocks.text: Low-ticket products live or die by fees. A **fixed fee** (taxa fixa) like R$2,49 is small on R$97 but big on R$9,90. Here is one R$27 front sale on each option. These numbers come **before** payout costs, FX spread and affiliate commission.

The EscalePay claim B row uses an **example exchange rate only**: USD 1 = R$5,50. Check the real rate on the day. The two EscalePay fee claims conflict, which is exactly why you ask support in writing and confirm it with your own test sale. Do this now: copy this table into your sheet and replace the claims with the real fee you see after your test.

blocks.title: Why the cheap bump never sells alone
blocks.text: If the R$9,90 'Desafio das 52 Semanas: Kit Poupança' were sold alone on Hotmart, the fee would be about R$0,98 + R$2,49 = R$3,47. That is about **35% of the price** gone. As an order bump in the same checkout as the R$27 front, it may share one transaction, so the fixed fee may hit only once. Check this on each platform. This is why the plan is a R$27 front plus bumps, and not cheap products sold alone.

Add one more line to your maths: affiliates. When an affiliate sells the R$27 front at 50%, R$13,50 goes to them (check whether it is calculated before or after fees). That is fine. You did not pay to find that customer, and the bump and upsell can still add to your side. Never judge an affiliate sale by the front price alone. Look at the **full order**.

A **refund** (reembolso) is when the buyer asks for the money back through the platform. In Brazil the buyer has 7 days to cancel an online purchase, and you honour it without arguing. A **chargeback** (contestação da compra no cartão) is different: the buyer disputes a card payment with their bank. Chargebacks can bring extra fees and put your account at risk, and how EscalePay handles them is still unknown. Your best protection is simple: a clear product, a clear page, fast delivery and polite, fast refunds.

blocks.title: Your money discipline
items: **Withdraw often.** When sales grow, withdraw every day.
**Never keep a big balance** on any platform. A balance is money you do not control yet.
Log every withdrawal: date, amount requested, MT received, days it took.
Keep a backup checkout on Hotmart for each front product, so you can swap the links in minutes.
Every week, back up your files, your sales export and your customer list (only people who gave consent) in two places.

blocks.text: Refund requests are data. If several buyers say the same thing, like 'não sabia que era digital' or 'o e-mail não chegou', fix the page or the delivery email. Do not blame the buyer. Do this now: add a 'refund reason' column to your sales sheet today, before the first refund arrives.

sections.heading: Legal basics: Brazil, Portugal and Mozambique

blocks.title: Brazil (your first market)
items: **CDC art. 49:** 7-day withdrawal right (direito de arrependimento). Honour every request made within 7 days.
**Decreto 7.962/2013:** show seller identification (name, identification such as your NUIT, contact). Check how a foreign seller should show it.
**LGPD:** a privacy policy (Política de Privacidade) in Portuguese, and clear consent before you send marketing messages.
**CDC art. 37 and 67 + CONAR:** no misleading ads, no guaranteed results or earnings. The finance products are educational, not investment advice.
**Devocional:** Bible references and paraphrase only, no verbatim quotes (the NVI is copyrighted).

blocks.title: Portugal and the EU (later)
items: 14-day withdrawal right, unless the buyer ticks an **express consent checkbox** to get the digital content immediately.

EU VAT applies from the **first B2C e-book sale** (B2C: sale to a normal consumer) for non-EU sellers, unless the platform is the **merchant of record** (the company legally responsible for the sale and the tax).
So: **do not price in EUR** until you have checked this.

blocks.title: Mozambique (where you live)
items: 16% VAT (IVA) on digital goods and services is reported. Check whether and how it applies to you.
**ISPC** is a simplified tax that may fit a small business. Check with the AT (Autoridade Tributária) or an accountant.
Banco de Moçambique **Aviso 1/GBM/2025** required 50% conversion of export earnings. It is temporary and possibly ending around Oct 2026. Check the current status.

blocks.text: I am your mentor, not your lawyer or your accountant. This list is a map of **questions**, not final answers. Book one hour with a Mozambican accountant (contabilista) before your income grows, and take the questions below with you.

blocks.title: Questions for your accountant
items: Should I register under ISPC or another regime for selling digital products abroad?
Does the reported 16% VAT apply to my sales to Brazilian buyers?
Is the 50% conversion rule (Aviso 1/GBM/2025) still in force, and how does it affect M-Pesa, e-Mola or bank payouts?
What records must I keep for each sale and each withdrawal?
How do I show my NUIT and identification correctly to foreign buyers?

blocks.title: E-mail para marcar a consulta com o contabilista (português de Moçambique)
blocks.text:
Bom dia, Senhor(a) [nome].
Chamo-me [o seu nome] e estou a começar um pequeno negócio de produtos digitais (e-books e planners em PDF), vendidos a clientes no Brasil através de plataformas internacionais. Os pagamentos chegam por M-Pesa, e-Mola ou conta bancária em meticais.
Gostaria de marcar uma consulta de uma hora para esclarecer o regime fiscal adequado (ISPC ou outro), o IVA, as regras do Banco de Moçambique sobre receitas de exportação e os registos que devo manter.
Poderia indicar-me a sua disponibilidade e o valor da consulta?
Com os melhores cumprimentos,
[o seu nome]
[telemóvel e e-mail de contacto]

key_takeaways: Platform claims are not facts: run real Pix and card tests and one real payout before you promote anything.
Set up Family 1 in BRL with front, bump, upsell, downsell and 50% affiliate commission on the front.
Know your fee maths: on a R$27 sale you keep roughly R$21,84 to R$24,30, depending on the platform and on which EscalePay claim is true, before payout costs and affiliates.
Withdraw often, never keep big balances, and keep Hotmart ready as a backup checkout.
Honour the 7-day refund, show seller identification, publish a privacy policy, and ask an accountant about ISPC, VAT and the FX rule.

quiz.question: What must happen before you send any traffic to your EscalePay checkout?
options: You publish 10 videos
A real Pix test, a real card test and one real payout all pass
You set the prices in EUR
You reach 100 followers
quiz.explanation: EscalePay's international selling is not independently verified, so real tests are the only proof that buyers can pay and the money reaches you.

quiz.question: On Hotmart (9.9% + R$2,49), about how much is the fee on one R$27 sale?
quiz.explanation: 9.9% of R$27 is about R$2,67. Add the fixed R$2,49 and the total fee is about R$5,16.

quiz.question: Why should you not price in EUR yet?
options: People in Portugal do not buy e-books
EU VAT can apply from the first B2C e-book sale for non-EU sellers unless the platform is the merchant of record
Pix only works in euros
The EU has no refund rules
quiz.explanation: Selling in the EU can create VAT duties from the very first sale. Check who is the merchant of record before you open EUR prices.

glossary.meaning: Checking who you are with ID and proof of address before a platform pays you.
Moving money from the platform to your M-Pesa, e-Mola or bank account.
When a buyer disputes a card payment with their bank instead of asking you for a refund.
The company that legally sells to the buyer and handles taxes such as VAT.
The buyer's right to cancel an online purchase: 7 days in Brazil, 14 in the EU unless the buyer gives express consent to get the content immediately.
The hidden difference between the real exchange rate and the rate you actually receive.

chapters.title: Sales Pages That Sell (Built With Lovable)
chapters.subtitle: One page, one promise, one button
chapters.mentor_intro: Your **sales page** (página de vendas) has one job. It must take a stranger from 'what is this?' to 'I want it' in under a minute, on a phone, often on weak mobile data. It is not a website. It is not a portfolio. It is one page, one promise, one button. The good news: you already have Lovable Pro, your own domains and ready-made Lovable prompts in the Family 1 launch kit. So you are not starting from a blank screen. You are assembling. In this chapter I will show you the anatomy of a low-ticket page for Brazil and the copy rules that keep it honest and clear. You will learn to build it in Lovable one step at a time, without wasting credits. Then we connect your domain, your EscalePay links, the thank-you and upsell pages, and the Meta Pixel. Finally, we test it the way a buyer would. A page that is live and tested beats a perfect page that only exists in your head.
learning_goals: Build a low-ticket sales page in the right order, from the hero promise to the sticky mobile button.
Write PT-BR copy that is specific, honest and easy to scan, with Claude drafting and you checking.
Use the Lovable prompts one step at a time, connect your domain and link every button to EscalePay.
Set up thank-you, upsell and downsell pages, legal pages and Meta Pixel events.
Test the page on a phone and with real people, and decide which step to fix first.

sections.heading: Anatomy of a R$27 page for Brazil

blocks.text: Your buyers will mostly arrive from a short video or a Pinterest pin, on a phone, curious but busy. They decide fast. So the page follows a fixed order, and each block answers the **next question in their head**. If a block does not answer a question, delete it. The **hero** (seção principal) is the first block: the big promise at the top of the page.

blocks.title: The 12 blocks, top to bottom
rows: What is in it for me?
Rotina, celular, pouco tempo a dois
What if I don't like it?
Fixed at the bottom on mobile

blocks.title: Hero e garantia (PT-BR, rascunho: ajuste ao conteúdo real do seu PDF)
blocks.text:
Título: 52 encontros prontos para vocês voltarem a se conectar, um por semana, o ano inteiro.
Subtítulo: Um caderno digital para imprimir, com ideias de encontros, perguntas para conversar e espaço para escrever juntos.
Botão: Quero meu Caderno do Casal por R$27
Garantia: Você tem 7 dias para conhecer o caderno. Se não for para vocês, é só pedir o reembolso dentro desse prazo.

Put the mockup and the button **above the fold** (primeira dobra: what you see before you scroll) on a phone screen. If someone must scroll to understand what you sell, you lose them. Show Pix clearly too: in 2025 Pix was 42% of Brazilian e-commerce value and cards were 40%. But show a payment badge only if your Chapter 4 tests proved the checkout accepts that method. If the checkout offers interest-free instalments (parcelamento sem juros), mention it, because instalments matter to Brazilian buyers. Check that it is really offered first.

sections.heading: Copy that is specific, honest and scannable

blocks.text: **Copy** (texto de vendas) means every word on the page. Good copy for a R$27 product is not clever. It is clear. Use these five rules to check every block.

blocks.title: Five copy rules
items: **Specific beats big:** '52 encontros' and '100 cartões' beat 'transforme seu relacionamento'.
**Honest beats hype:** no promise to save a marriage, no guaranteed results.
**Scannable:** short lines, one idea per paragraph, bold key words, bullets for the contents.
**One reader, in PT-BR:** use 'você', everyday Brazilian words, a warm tone.
**Show, don't claim:** real page previews sell more than adjectives.

blocks.title: Weak vs strong headline (example)
blocks.text: Weak: 'O melhor caderno para casais do Brasil!' It is vague, and it is an unproven ranking. Strong: 'Um encontro pronto por semana: 52 ideias e perguntas para conversar a dois.' The strong one tells the buyer exactly what they get. Only use details that are really inside your PDF.

No fake testimonials. No fake 'só hoje' countdown timers. No invented 'de R$197 por R$27'. The only **anchor** (preço de referência) you use is an honest one, like the Mega Kit's real total of R$207,60. Fake proof can break Brazilian consumer law (CDC art. 37) and Meta's ad rules, and when buyers notice, the refunds follow.

Let Claude write the first draft of every block. Then you check three things, line by line: **Is it true? Is it clear? Are the PT-BR words and accents right?** Claude is fast. You are responsible. That split is your superpower as a one-person business. Do this now: print or open the Family 1 sales copy from your launch kit and mark every line with a tick (true and clear) or a cross (fix it).

sections.heading: Building it in Lovable Pro, one step at a time

blocks.text: Lovable builds pages from your **prompts** (instruções em texto). Each message uses **credits** (créditos) from your Pro plan, so check your balance in your account before you start. Big messy prompts that you fix five times cost more than small, clear ones. Your Family 1 launch kit already has the prompts in order. Use them like Lego: one piece, check, next piece.

blocks.title: The build loop
items: Create a new Lovable project called 'caderno-do-casal'.
Paste **prompt 1 only** (structure and style). Wait for the preview.
Check the preview in mobile view first, then desktop. Write down what is wrong.
Fix it with one short, specific prompt. Do not paste the next prompt until this step looks right.
Paste the next prompt (hero, then what's inside, offer, FAQ and so on). Check and fix again.
Replace every **placeholder** (conteúdo provisório) with your real images: mockups and page previews.
Read every word on the preview: accents, prices, product names.
Publish.

blocks.title: A good fix prompt (example)
blocks.text: Bad: 'Make it better.' Good: 'On mobile, the mockup image is below the button. Move the mockup above the headline, keep the button visible without scrolling, and **do not change any other section**.' That last sentence saves you credits and surprises.
If Lovable breaks something that was working, go back to an earlier version instead of writing three prompts to repair it. Find where version history is in your Lovable project before you need it.

sections.heading: Domain, checkout links and the pages after the purchase

blocks.title: Connect everything
items: Open the project settings in Lovable and find the custom domain option (menu names can change). Add a **subdomain** (subdomínio), for example casal.seudominio.com.
Copy the **DNS records** (registros DNS) that Lovable shows. Add them where you bought the domain, then wait until Lovable shows the domain as connected.
Paste each EscalePay checkout URL into **every** buy button: hero, offer block, final CTA and sticky button.
Click every button on the live page and confirm it opens the right product at the right price.
Set the after-purchase flow in EscalePay: upsell page, then downsell page, then thank-you page. Ask support in writing how its one-click upsell works with pages built outside EscalePay, and test it.

blocks.title: Meta Pixel events (eventos do pixel): set up now, use for ads later
items: **PageView:** someone opened a page.
**ViewContent:** someone saw the product on the sales page.
**InitiateCheckout:** someone clicked a buy button.
**Purchase:** someone paid. It must fire only once, on the thank-you page or inside EscalePay. Check which option EscalePay supports.

blocks.text: You will not run ads yet. Ads come only after organic sales. But install the Pixel now, so it collects data from your organic visitors. Ask Lovable to add your Pixel ID to every page and an InitiateCheckout event to every buy button. Say in your privacy policy that the page uses the Meta Pixel. On the thank-you page, give clear access steps and your support email, so buyers never feel lost.

sections.heading: Fast pages, light images, legal footer

blocks.title: Image workflow
items: Generate the art in Gemini **without any text**. AI image tools often break Portuguese accents like ç, ã and é.
Add titles and prices in Canva, then export.
Compress every image before you upload it, with a free online compressor. Use WebP format if you can.
Make every mockup show your **real cover and real pages**. Never show invented AI pages that are not in the PDF.

blocks.title: Legal pages (link them in the footer)
items: **Política de Privacidade** (LGPD), in Portuguese: what data you collect and why.
**Termos de Uso** and **Política de Reembolso**: the 7-day withdrawal right (CDC art. 49).
**Seller identification** (Decreto 7.962/2013): name, identification and contact email. Check how a foreign seller should show it.
For the Planner Financeiro page later: 'conteúdo educativo, não é recomendação de investimento'.
A consent checkbox before you collect emails or WhatsApp numbers for marketing.

blocks.text: Ask Claude to draft each legal page using your real details, then read every line. A copied template that mentions a company you are not is worse than no template.

sections.heading: Test like a buyer, then fix the right thing first

blocks.title: The 10-point QA (checagem de qualidade)
items: 1. The page loads fast on your phone, on mobile data.
2. Hero and mockup are visible without scrolling.
3. Every buy button opens the right EscalePay checkout.
4. Price on the page = price on the checkout (R$27).
5. The bump appears on the checkout.
6. After a test purchase, upsell, downsell and thank-you pages appear in order.
7. No typos, and every accent is correct.
8. Legal pages open from the footer.
9. The sticky button shows on mobile and does not cover text.
10. The Pixel fires (check with Meta's testing tools).

blocks.title: The 5-second test and the friend test
blocks.text: **5-second test:** show the page on your phone to someone for 5 seconds, then hide it. Ask: 'What does it sell? Who is it for? How much?' If they cannot answer, fix the hero before anything else. **Friend test:** ask a friend to go through the purchase on their own phone while you watch in silence. Every pause or question shows you a problem.

**Conversion** (conversão) has steps: visitors, then checkout, then purchase. Example only, invented numbers: 500 visitors, 40 open the checkout (40 ÷ 500 = 8%), 12 buy (12 ÷ 40 = 30%). There is no official 'right' rate, so compare your own numbers week by week. Then **fix the weakest step first.** If few people click to the checkout, work on the hero, the mockup and the offer. If many reach the checkout but do not pay, look at the checkout itself: the price and currency shown, whether Pix is visible, trust signals and language.
Live and tested beats perfect and hidden.

key_takeaways: A low-ticket page follows a fixed order: hero promise, mockup, problem, solution, contents, offer, payment badges, guarantee, FAQ, final CTA, sticky button.
Copy must be specific, honest and scannable, and use only honest anchors like the real R$207,60 total.
Build in Lovable one prompt at a time: check the preview on mobile, fix with small, precise prompts.
Connect the domain, link every button to EscalePay, set up the upsell, downsell and thank-you pages, the legal pages and the Pixel.
Test with the 10-point QA, the 5-second test and the friend test, then fix the weakest step of the funnel first.

Replace placeholders with real mockups and page previews (Gemini art without text, words added in Canva, compressed).
Connect your custom domain and link every buy button to the EscalePay checkout.
Create the thank-you, upsell (R$27) and downsell (R$17) pages, plus the privacy, terms and refund pages.
Install the Meta Pixel and run the 10-point QA on your phone.
Ask 3 people to do the 5-second test and write down their answers.
challenge.proof: The live URL, your 10-point QA with every box ticked, and the 3 five-second-test answers.
challenge.bonus: Ask one friend to do a full friend test (purchase and refund) on their own phone while you watch without helping. Write down every moment they hesitate, and fix the top one.

quiz.question: What should a visitor see on a phone before scrolling?
options: The hero promise, the mockup and the buy button
The FAQ
The legal pages
The full list of all 9 products
quiz.explanation: Buyers decide fast. If the promise, the product image and the button are not above the fold, many leave before they understand the offer.

quiz.question: Many visitors open the checkout but few pay. What do you fix first?
options: The hero headline
The checkout: price and currency shown, Pix, trust and language
The number of videos you post
The product itself
quiz.explanation: The page is doing its job by sending people to the checkout. The leak is at the payment step, so you fix that step first.

quiz.question: What is the smartest way to use your Lovable credits?
options: Paste all prompts in one huge message
One prompt at a time, check the preview, then fix with small, specific prompts
Regenerate the whole page every time something is wrong
Skip the mobile view to save time
quiz.explanation: Small, clear steps cost fewer credits and give you control. Big messy prompts lead to many expensive fixes.

chapters.title: The Faceless Content Machine
chapters.subtitle: Content you make in batches, without your face or your voice
chapters.mentor_intro: You want 'sales every minute'. I love that energy, so let me be honest with you. One sale a minute is 1,440 sales a day. That is top-product territory, built with big ad budgets or armies of affiliates. The honest path starts smaller: the first sale, then 10 a day, then 100 a day. And the engine that gets you up those first steps for zero cash is **content**. Not your face. Not your voice. A **perfil dark** (faceless profile) that shows the product doing its job: pages flipping, a printer working, a question that makes a couple laugh. In this chapter you will choose your accounts and platforms, learn the formats that sell journals and printables, and write hooks in PT-BR. Then you will build a batching workflow where one 3-hour session gives you 15 posts. You will also learn the rules that can kill your reach overnight. Finally, you will measure the chain from views to sales, so you stop guessing. Content is not magic. It is a machine. Let's build it.
learning_goals: Choose your perfil dark setup and the right platforms for each product family.
Create formats and PT-BR hooks that sell journals and printables without your face or voice.
Batch 15 posts in one 3-hour session with Claude, Gemini, Canva and CapCut.
Post 3-5 times a day while respecting the unoriginal-content, AI-label and licence rules.
Measure views, profile visits, link clicks and sales, and fix the weakest step first.

sections.heading: Perfil dark: your accounts and platforms

blocks.text: You have two options: one **umbrella brand** (marca guarda-chuva) for everything, or **one brand account per family**. My advice: one account per family on TikTok and Instagram. Couples, people fixing their finances and teachers are three different audiences. An account that talks to one kind of person is easier to understand, for people and for the algorithm (o algoritmo). Start with Family 1 only. On Pinterest, one account with a board per family is fine. Your **bio link** (link na bio) always goes to the Lovable sales page.

blocks.title: Where to post
rows: Label realistic AI people or scenes
Planners, printables; women 18+ ~64% of BR users
Real page previews, link to your page
Only people who chose to join

blocks.text: Name each account after the benefit, not after you. Example names only: '@cadernodocasal' or '@encontrosadois'. Check that the name is free on all platforms on the same day, and use the same logo, colours and bio everywhere. WhatsApp has 120M+ users in Brazil, so open a channel early and invite your followers to join it. Never add people to it without their choice.

sections.heading: Formats that sell journals and printables

blocks.title: Six faceless formats
items: **PDF flip-through** (folheando o PDF): screen-record yourself scrolling the pages, with text on screen.
**Printing ASMR** (ASMR: calm, satisfying sounds): the printer printing the pages, with the real sound and no voice. Show your hands only if you are comfortable, never your face.
**POV** (point of view, ponto de vista): 'POV: vocês finalmente têm um encontro por semana sem precisar pensar'.
**Text-on-screen lists:** '5 ideias de encontro em casa para este fim de semana'.
**Carousels** (carrossel) on Instagram and Pinterest: 5-8 slides with real page previews.
**Questions from the product:** one card from '100 Cartões de Perguntas para Casais' per video, with 'responda nos comentários'.

blocks.title: Five Family 1 posts (example)
blocks.text: 1) A flip-through of 8 pages of the Caderno with the text 'olha o encontro da semana 12'. 2) Printing ASMR of the 100 cartões. 3) POV: 'vocês, sexta à noite, sem celular, com uma pergunta difícil'. 4) A list: '3 perguntas para fazer ao seu amor hoje'. 5) A carousel: 'como funciona o Caderno do Casal', with 6 real pages and R$27 on the last slide.

For the Devocional do Casal, show Bible **references and your own paraphrase**, never long verbatim quotes (the NVI translation is copyrighted). And never promise results in your content. 'Salve seu casamento em 30 dias' is a promise you cannot keep, and it breaks the honesty rules you follow everywhere else.

A **hook** (gancho) is the first line on screen and the first second of the video. If it fails, nothing else matters. Use a simple formula: **who it is for + a pain or a desire + a reason to keep watching** (a number, a question or a surprise). Not every hook needs all three parts, but the strongest ones usually have them.

blocks.title: Ganchos prontos para a Família 1 (PT-BR)
blocks.text:
1. Casais que só conversam sobre boletos: isso é pra vocês.
2. 52 ideias de encontro para o ano inteiro, e a primeira é dentro de casa.
3. Faça essa pergunta hoje à noite e veja o que acontece.
4. Se o celular está jantando com vocês, salva esse vídeo.
5. O presente de aniversário de namoro que ninguém espera.
6. Responde aqui: qual foi o primeiro filme que vocês viram juntos?

Ask Claude for 20 hooks per product, then keep the 10 that sound like a real Brazilian friend talking, not like a billboard. Read each one in your head. If it sounds like an ad, rewrite it. Then watch which hooks keep people watching (the platform shows this as watch time or retention, retenção). That number teaches you more than likes do.

sections.heading: The 3-hour batch: 15 posts in one session

blocks.text: **Batching** (produção em lote) means you make many posts in one focused session instead of one post a day. This is how one person can post 3-5 times a day without burning out. Your 30-day calendar from the Family 1 launch kit already tells you what to make. You just produce it in blocks of time.

blocks.title: One 3-hour session
rows: Pick 15 calendar ideas; Claude drafts hooks and captions
Gemini art (no text), Canva covers and slides
Record flip-throughs and printing; edit in CapCut
Check accents and AI labels; schedule

blocks.title: Batch workflow
items: Open the Family 1 30-day calendar and copy the next 15 ideas into your sheet.
Ask Claude for a hook, on-screen text and a caption with a **call to action** (chamada para ação) for each idea.
Generate background art in Gemini without text, then add all the words in Canva.
Record all the flip-throughs and printing clips in one go, then edit all 15 in CapCut with one template.
Check every post: accents, price, product name, and music from the platform's own library that is allowed for your account type (check this in the app).
Schedule the posts or save them as drafts, with the planned time written in your sheet.

blocks.text: Build one CapCut template (fonts, colours, an end card that says 'link na bio') and reuse it every time. The same look every time means faster editing and a brand people start to recognise.

sections.heading: Posting, replies and the rules that protect your reach

blocks.title: Daily rhythm
items: Post **3-5 times a day across platforms**, for example 1-2 TikToks, 1 Reel, 1 Short and 1-2 pins. Do not post 5 times on one platform.
Keep your bio link pointing to the Lovable sales page.
Reply to comments the same day. When a question is good, answer it with a new video.
Answer DMs (mensagens diretas) with a friendly script. Never message people who did not ask.

blocks.title: Resposta para DM e comentário (PT-BR)
blocks.text: Oi! Que bom que você gostou. O Caderno do Casal é digital: você recebe o PDF no e-mail logo depois do pagamento e pode imprimir em casa. São 52 encontros, um por semana. O link está na bio do perfil. Se ficar com alguma dúvida, é só me chamar aqui.

blocks.title: Rules that can kill your reach
blocks.text: YouTube stopped paying for mass-produced 'inauthentic' faceless content (15 Jul 2025). Shorts still bring traffic, but make each one original. Facebook cuts the reach of reposted or unoriginal content (14 Jul 2025), so use your own product footage, not other people's videos. TikTok requires AI labels on realistic AI people or scenes, so turn the label on when you use them. If you ever use an AI voice: the ElevenLabs free plan has **no commercial licence**, and you need the Starter plan (~USD 5-6/month) for business use. Text on screen plus library music works fine with no voice at all.

sections.heading: Measure the chain: views to sales

blocks.text: Views do not pay you. Sales do. Track the four links of the chain every day in one Google Sheet, so you can see exactly where it breaks. For each step, calculate a simple percentage: this number divided by the number in the step before.

blocks.title: Reading the chain (fictional numbers)
blocks.text: Day 3, example only: 9,000 views, 180 profile visits, 45 link clicks, 2 sales. The percentages: 180 ÷ 9,000 = 2% visit the profile; 45 ÷ 180 = 25% click the link; 2 ÷ 45 = about 4% buy. There is no official 'good' number, so compare with your own posts. Say your flip-through videos usually bring 4% profile visits and this list video brought only 2%. Then this video entertains without making people curious about the product. The fix: more flip-throughs that show real pages, and a clear 'o caderno completo está no link da bio' at the end of each video.
Make it, post it, measure it, fix one thing. Repeat.

key_takeaways: Start with one faceless brand account for Family 1, with the bio link going to your Lovable sales page.
Make the product the star: flip-throughs, printing ASMR, POV, lists, carousels and real questions from the product.
A hook = who it is for + a pain or desire + a reason to keep watching.
One 3-hour batch gives you 15 posts; post 3-5 times a day across platforms.
Stay original, label realistic AI, and use an AI voice only with a commercial licence.
Track views, profile visits, link clicks and sales, and fix the weakest step first.

challenge.title: Content engine
challenge.mission: Create your Family 1 faceless accounts, batch 15 posts in one session, publish them over 3 days and track every number.
challenge.time_box: 4 days (one 3-hour batch session + 3 days of posting)
steps: Create the Family 1 accounts on TikTok, Instagram and Pinterest, with the same name, logo and bio link to your sales page.
Copy 15 ideas from the Family 1 30-day calendar into a sheet.
Batch all 15 posts in one 3-hour session with Claude, Gemini (no text), Canva and CapCut.
Check accents, prices, AI labels and music before you schedule.
Post or schedule the 15 posts over 3 days, about 5 a day across platforms.
Reply to every comment and DM within the same day.
Fill the tracking sheet every day: views, profile visits, link clicks and sales per post.
challenge.proof: Your tracking sheet with 15 rows filled across 3 days, plus links to your 3 most-viewed posts.
challenge.bonus: Turn your best hook into 3 new versions, post them on day 4 and compare the numbers with the original.

quiz.question: Which hook follows the formula 'who + pain or desire + reason to keep watching'?
options: Compre agora!
Casais que só conversam sobre boletos: faça essa pergunta hoje à noite
Novo vídeo
Meu produto é o melhor
quiz.explanation: It names who it is for (couples), touches a real pain (only talking about bills) and gives a reason to keep watching (a question to try tonight).

quiz.question: What is true about using an AI voice in your videos?
options: Any free AI voice can be used commercially
The ElevenLabs free plan has no commercial licence; the Starter plan is needed for business use
AI voices are banned on all platforms
You must use your own voice
quiz.explanation: The free ElevenLabs plan has no commercial licence. Use the paid Starter plan, or skip voice and use text on screen.

quiz.question: Your videos get many views but very few profile visits. What is the most likely problem?
options: The checkout is broken
The content entertains but does not make people curious about the product
The price is too high
You post too few pins
quiz.explanation: The break is between views and profile visits, so the content needs to show the product more and give a clear reason to visit the profile.

glossary.meaning: A brand account that never shows the creator's face or voice.
The first line or second of a post, made to stop the scroll.
Making many posts in one focused session instead of one at a time.
